title: Instar SlackAdapter Spec v1.2 (Round 2 Addressed)
markdown:
# Instar SlackAdapter — Technical Specification

**Version**: 1.2
**Date**: 2026-03-28
**Authors**: Echo + Justin
**Status**: Draft — Post-Review Revision (Round 1 + Round 2 findings addressed)

---

## 1. Overview

### 1.1 Purpose

Add native Slack support as a first-class messaging adapter in Instar, on par with TelegramAdapter. Each user creates their own Slack app (DIY model) — no shared infrastructure, no published app, no third-party token custody. The setup wizard automates the entire process via browser automation (Playwright/Chrome), requiring only that the user log into Slack.

### 1.2 Goals

1. **Feature parity with Telegram** where Slack's platform allows (~80% coverage)
2. **Single manual step setup** — user logs into Slack; agent automates everything else
3. **DIY app model** — each user creates and owns their Slack app, matching Telegram's BotFather self-contained model
4. **Socket Mode** — no public URLs, no webhooks, no infrastructure. Local-first like Telegram's long polling
5. **Zero external SDK** — direct HTTP calls to Slack Web API, matching the project's zero-SDK pattern
6. **Implement `MessagingAdapter` interface** — drop-in alongside Telegram and WhatsApp
7. **Reuse shared infrastructure** — MessageLogger, SessionChannelRegistry, StallDetector, CommandRouter, AuthGate, MessagingEventBus

### 1.3 Non-Goals

- Publishing a Slack app to the App Directory (requires shared infrastructure, token custody, compliance — antithetical to instar's local-first philosophy)
- Replacing TelegramAdapter (Telegram's forum topics are a better UX for topic-per-conversation)
- Supporting Slack's Events API via webhooks (requires public URL — conflicts with local-first)
- Using `@slack/bolt` or `@slack/socket-mode` SDK (zero-SDK pattern)

### 1.4 Key Architectural Decision: DIY App Model

**Why not publish a Slack app?**

| Concern | Published App | DIY App |
|---------|--------------|---------|
| Infrastructure | Must run OAuth callback server (HTTPS, public, persistent) | None |
| Token custody | Publisher holds all users' bot tokens | User holds their own token |
| Security liability | Compromise exposes all users | Compromise is self-contained |
| Compliance | Privacy policy, ToS, Slack review, ongoing obligations | None |
| Maintenance | API deprecations affect all users simultaneously | Each user manages their own |
| Philosophy | SaaS model — shared infrastructure | Local-first — self-contained |

The DIY model is the exact equivalent of Telegram's BotFather approach: each user creates their own bot, holds their own token, no middleman.

---

## 2. Feature Mapping

### 2.1 Telegram → Slack Equivalence

| Feature | Telegram | Slack | Equivalence | Notes |
|---------|----------|-------|-------------|-------|
| Message intake | Long polling (`getUpdates`) | Socket Mode (WebSocket) | **Full** | Slack is better — real-time, no offset tracking |
| Conversation streams | Forum topics | Channels | **Partial** | Different UX model — see Channel Strategy |
| Send to conversation | `sendMessage` + `thread_id` | `chat.postMessage` + `channel` | **Full** | |
| Create conversations | `createForumTopic` | `conversations.create` | **Partial** | Naming restrictions (lowercase, no emoji) |
| Archive/close | `closeForumTopic` | `conversations.archive` | **Full** | |
| Voice messages | Native `.ogg` + transcription | No equivalent | **None** | Accept audio file uploads as generic files |
| Photos | `photo` type | `file_shared` event | **Full** | |
| Documents | `document` (20MB limit) | `file_shared` (1GB paid) | **Full** | Slack is better on size limits |
| Interactive buttons | `InlineKeyboardMarkup` | Block Kit `actions` | **Full** | Slack is much richer |
| Callbacks | `callback_query` | Interaction payloads (Socket Mode) | **Full** | |
| Message editing | `editMessageText` | `chat.update` | **Full** | |
| User auth | Numeric user ID allowlist | String user ID + workspace membership | **Full** | Workspace is additional gate |
| File download | `getFile` + token URL | `url_private` + bearer header | **Full** | |
| Reactions | Very limited | Full `reactions.*` API | **Slack better** | New capability |
| Rich formatting | MarkdownV2/HTML | mrkdwn + Block Kit | **Full** | Block Kit is significantly richer |
| Rate limits | ~30/sec same chat | ~1/sec (tier-based) | **Partial** | Slack more restrictive |
| Silent sends | `disable_notification` | No sender-side control | **Partial** | |
| Pins | `pinChatMessage` | `pins.add` | **Full** | |

### 2.2 New Capabilities (Slack-Only)

| Feature | Description | Use Case |
|---------|-------------|----------|
| **Reactions as acknowledgment** | `reactions.add` with `eyes` when processing, `white_check_mark` when done | Replace text-based ack pattern |
| **Block Kit interactive messages** | Buttons, dropdowns, date pickers, modals | Richer Prompt Gate experience |
| **Ephemeral messages** | `chat.postEphemeral` — visible only to one user | Status updates without noise |
| **User presence** | `users.getPresence` — know if user is online | Smart notification timing |
| **Scheduled messages** | `chat.scheduleMessage` — send at a future time | Delayed notifications |
| **Channel sections** | Sidebar organization via `usergroups` | Group agent channels visually |

### 2.3 Lost Capabilities (Telegram-Only)

| Feature | Impact | Mitigation |
|---------|--------|------------|
| **Voice messages** | Medium — loses tap-to-talk UX | Accept audio file uploads; offer transcription if audio received |
| **Topic emoji/color** | Low — cosmetic | Channel naming conventions with prefixes |
| **Single-group UX** | Medium — channel sprawl vs topic list | Naming conventions, aggressive archiving, workspace isolation |
| **Silent sends** | Low — edge case | Post to low-priority channels user has muted |
| **Burst rate** | Low — agent rarely needs 30 msg/sec | Batching, rate-aware sending |

---

## 3. Architecture

### 3.1 System Position

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Instar Server                         │
│                                                          │
│  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  │
│  │ Telegram     │  │ WhatsApp     │  │ Slack        │  │
│  │ Adapter      │  │ Adapter      │  │ Adapter      │  │
│  │ (poll-based) │  │ (Baileys/API)│  │ (WebSocket)  │  │
│  └──────┬───────┘  └──────┬───────┘  └──────┬───────┘  │
│         │                 │                 │            │
│         └────────┬────────┴────────┬────────┘            │
│                  │                 │                      │
│         ┌───────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐              │
│         │AdapterRegistry│  │SharedModules │              │
│         └───────────────┘  │ MessageLogger│              │
│                            │ StallDetector│              │
│                            │ CommandRouter│              │
│                            │ AuthGate     │              │
│                            │ EventBus     │              │
│                            └──────────────┘              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

External:
  Telegram Bot API ← TelegramAdapter (long-polling)
  WhatsApp         ← WhatsAppAdapter (Baileys/Business API)
  Slack Web API    ← SlackAdapter (Socket Mode WebSocket)
```

### 3.2 Message Flow

**Inbound (Slack → Instar):**

```
User sends message in Slack channel
  → Slack delivers via Socket Mode WebSocket
  → SlackAdapter receives event (type: message)
  → Convert to Instar Message format
  → AuthGate checks user authorization
  → CommandRouter checks for /commands
  → Route to SessionChannelRegistry → target session
  → Inject into tmux session as [slack:CHANNEL_ID] prefix
```

**Outbound (Instar → Slack):**

```
Session generates response
  → slack-reply.sh CHANNEL_ID "message text"
  → POST /slack/reply/CHANNEL_ID on Instar server
  → SlackAdapter.send() called
  → POST https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage
  → Message appears in Slack channel
```

### 3.3 Socket Mode Implementation

Socket Mode uses a WebSocket connection instead of HTTP webhooks. No public URL needed.

**Connection flow:**
1. Call `POST https://slack.com/api/apps.connections.open` with app-level token (`xapp-...`)
2. Receive a WebSocket URL (wss://wss-primary.slack.com/...)
3. Open WebSocket connection
4. Receive events as JSON payloads
5. Acknowledge each event with `{"envelope_id": "..."}` within 3 seconds
6. Handle disconnections with automatic reconnection + exponential backoff

**Event types to handle:**

| Event | Slack Type | Action |
|-------|-----------|--------|
| New message | `message.channels` / `message.groups` | Route to session |
| File shared | `file_shared` | Download, process, route |
| Reaction added | `reaction_added` | Log, optionally act on |
| App mention | `app_mention` | Route to session |
| Interaction (button press) | `interactive` (via Socket Mode) | Handle Prompt Gate response |

**Reconnection strategy (hardened):**

Socket Mode WebSocket connections can silently stop delivering messages (socket appears open, no close event fires). This is a documented production issue. The reconnection strategy must handle both visible and silent failures.

- **On WebSocket close**: exponential backoff from first attempt (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, max 60s). Never reconnect immediately — prevents `apps.connections.open` rate limit exhaustion.
- **On `disconnect` event**: read the `reason` field. If `too_many_websockets`, wait 30s before reconnecting. If `refresh_requested`, reconnect immediately (Slack container rotation).
- **On `apps.connections.open` failure**: if `invalid_auth`, stop reconnecting (permanent failure — log error, alert user). If transient, apply backoff.
- **Active heartbeat**: if no events or pings received for 60s, the connection is presumed dead. Proactively close and reconnect. This catches silent failures that close-event reconnection misses.
- **Proactive rotation**: read `approximate_connection_time` from Slack's connection payload. Initiate graceful reconnect before Slack's container recycling forces a hard close.
- **Keep-alive**: respond to Slack's ping frames.
- **Message queuing during reconnect**: outbound messages are queued in memory during backoff/reconnect. Drained on successful reconnection. Queue cap: 100 messages (oldest dropped if exceeded).

**Post-acknowledgment exception guard:**
```typescript
// Acknowledge FIRST (must be within 3 seconds)
if (envelope.envelope_id) {
  this.ws?.send(JSON.stringify({ envelope_id: envelope.envelope_id }));
}
// Process SECOND — wrapped in try/catch so ack'd events don't silently fail
try {
  await this.handleSocketEvent(envelope);
} catch (err) {
  console.error('[slack] Event processing failed after ack:', err);
  // Event was ack'd — Slack won't redeliver. Log for debugging.
}
```

### 3.4 Socket Mode Reliability (vs Telegram Lifeline)

Telegram requires a separate Lifeline process because long polling is fragile — if the poller dies, messages are missed until offset-aware restart.

Socket Mode is architecturally more resilient:
- WebSocket reconnection with active heartbeat catches both visible and silent failures
- Slack buffers unacknowledged events and re-delivers on reconnect (~30 min window)
- No offset tracking needed — Slack manages delivery state

**However**, Socket Mode has known production reliability issues (documented by Slack and community). The "No Lifeline Needed" claim from v1.0 is retracted. Instead:

- **Phase 1**: Active heartbeat validation within the adapter (not just socket state — validate message flow). LaunchAgent/systemd auto-restart for server process death.
- **Phase 2**: If production experience shows the heartbeat is insufficient, build a lightweight Slack Lifeline process modeled on `TelegramLifeline.ts`.

The 30-minute retry window is acceptable for personal agent use. The active heartbeat is the critical defense against the more common failure mode (silent connection death).

---

## 4. Configuration

### 4.1 Config Schema

```typescript
export interface SlackConfig {
  /** Bot token (xoxb-...) — from OAuth installation */
  botToken: string;

  /** App-level token (xapp-...) — for Socket Mode connection */
  appToken: string;

  /** Workspace ID (T...) — for reference */
  workspaceId?: string;

  /** Workspace name — for display */
  workspaceName?: string;

  /** Authorized Slack user IDs (U...) — REQUIRED, deny-all if empty.
   *  Must contain at least one user ID. Setup wizard populates this
   *  from the installing user's Slack profile. */
  authorizedUserIds: string[];

  /** Audio file transcription provider (for uploaded audio files) */
  audioTranscriptionProvider?: 'groq' | 'openai';

  /** Stall detection timeout in minutes */
  stallTimeoutMinutes?: number;

  /** Promise follow-through timeout in minutes */
  promiseTimeoutMinutes?: number;

  /** Channel IDs for system channels */
  lifelineChannelId?: string;
  dashboardChannelId?: string;

  /** Message log retention in days. Default: 90 (matches Slack free plan history).
   *  Logs older than this are purged automatically on server startup
   *  and daily via a background task in MessageLogger.
   *  Set to 0 for unlimited (not recommended — GDPR compliance typically
   *  requires a defined retention limit). */
  logRetentionDays?: number;

  /** Prompt Gate config */
  promptGate?: {
    ownerId?: string;
    relayTimeoutSeconds?: number;
  };
}
```

**Security: `authorizedUserIds` is required and fail-closed.** If the array is empty, the adapter rejects ALL messages. This prevents accidental exposure in shared workspaces. The setup wizard MUST populate this during Step 12 (Extract Workspace Info).

### 4.2 Config Example

```json
{
  "messaging": [
    {
      "type": "slack",
      "enabled": true,
      "config": {
        "botToken": "xoxb-1234567890-1234567890123-abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwx",
        "appToken": "xapp-1-A1234567890-1234567890123-abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz1234567890abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz12",
        "workspaceId": "T1234567890",
        "workspaceName": "echo-agent",
        "authorizedUserIds": ["U1234567890"],
        "stallTimeoutMinutes": 5,
        "promiseTimeoutMinutes": 10,
        "lifelineChannelId": "C1234567890",
        "dashboardChannelId": "C0987654321",
        "promptGate": {
          "ownerId": "U1234567890",
          "relayTimeoutSeconds": 300
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

---

## 5. Channel Strategy

### 5.1 The Channel Sprawl Problem

Telegram's forum topics are ideal for instar: one group, many topics, clean navigation. Slack channels are independent — 50 channels is noisier than 50 topics.

### 5.2 Naming Convention

All agent channels use a prefix to group them visually and avoid collisions:

```
{agent-name}-{category}-{descriptor}

Categories:
  sys    — System channels (lifeline, dashboard, attention)
  job    — Job channels (ci-monitor, daily-summary)
  sess   — Session channels (conversation threads)
  attn   — Attention items
```

Examples:
```
echo-sys-lifeline        (replaces Lifeline topic)
echo-sys-dashboard       (replaces Dashboard topic)
echo-sys-attention       (replaces Attention topic)
echo-job-ci-monitor      (replaces CI Monitor job topic)
echo-job-daily-summary   (replaces Daily Summary job topic)
echo-sess-slack-review   (replaces per-conversation topic)
echo-attn-deploy-fail    (replaces per-attention-item topic)
```

### 5.3 Channel Lifecycle

| Action | When | Method |
|--------|------|--------|
| **Create system channels** | Setup / first boot | `conversations.create` — idempotent (check if exists first) |
| **Create job channels** | Job scheduler startup | `conversations.create` — one per job |
| **Create session channels** | New conversation / `/new` command | `conversations.create` — dynamically |
| **Create attention channels** | Attention item created | `conversations.create` — one per item |
| **Archive session channels** | Session ends or conversation stale | `conversations.archive` — reversible |
| **Unarchive** | Session resumed or conversation reopened | `conversations.unarchive` |

### 5.4 Channel Limits and Housekeeping

- Slack free plan: unlimited channels (this is not a constraint)
- Active channels should be kept under ~30 to avoid sidebar clutter
- Archive aggressively: any channel inactive for >7 days → auto-archive
- Job channels: reuse across runs (don't create new channel per run)
- Attention items: archive when status changes to DONE or WONT_DO

### 5.5 Workspace Setup

**Default: Dedicated workspace** — the wizard prompts the user: "I recommend creating a dedicated workspace for your agent. This keeps things clean and avoids privacy concerns with colleagues. Would you like me to create a dedicated workspace, or install into an existing one?"

If dedicated (recommended):
- Wizard creates a workspace named `{agent-name}-agent` (e.g., `echo-agent`)
- System channels created immediately
- The workspace serves as the equivalent of Telegram's supergroup
- Privacy is simpler — only the operator is in the workspace
- Free plan 90-day history limit applies — JSONL log is authoritative

If existing workspace (user's choice):
- Agent channels prefixed with agent name to avoid collisions
- Third-party awareness notice posted in each channel (see Section 6.7)
- `authorizedUserIds` becomes critical — must be populated to prevent other workspace members from commanding the agent
- User is warned: "Other workspace members may see the agent's channels. The agent will only respond to authorized users."

### 5.6 DM Support (Phase 1)

Direct messages are supported in Phase 1. DMs route to the lifeline session by default (configurable).

**Why DMs in Phase 1**: For first-time Slack users, messaging the bot via DM is the natural instinct. Requiring users to find the right channel first creates unnecessary friction.

**Routing**: DMs from authorized users → lifeline session. DMs from unauthorized users → rejected (fail-closed).

**Privacy note**: DM content enters the same JSONL message log as channel messages. DMs carry higher sensitivity expectations — users treat DMs as more private than channel messages. The unified log should acknowledge this. Consider: `logRetentionDays` may warrant a shorter value for DM content in future versions, but for v1 the unified log with configurable retention is acceptable.

### 5.7 Thread Support

Conversations within channels use Slack threads to keep channels readable. Every AI-in-Slack integration (Claude for Slack, ChatGPT for Slack) uses threads — this is what Slack users expect.

**Thread model:**
- New user messages in a channel start a new thread (bot replies in-thread)
- Subsequent messages in the same thread are routed to the same session context
- Thread `ts` is tracked in `SessionChannelRegistry` alongside channel ID
- **All thread replies go through AuthGate** — unauthorized users replying in a bot's thread are silently ignored. This applies equally to top-level messages and thread replies. The `handleMessage` method applies AuthGate before routing regardless of whether `thread_ts` is present.
- Cross-channel thread monitoring is deferred to Phase 2

---

## 6. Setup Wizard — Browser Automation

### 6.1 Overview

The setup wizard automates Slack setup via browser (Playwright or Chrome extension), matching the Telegram setup's single-manual-step experience. The user's only manual action is logging into Slack.

### 6.2 Pre-Setup Detection

Same waterfall as Telegram:
```
A. Playwright (preferred) → browser_navigate("about:blank")
B. Claude in Chrome (fallback) → tabs_context_mcp()
C. Manual (last resort) → conversational walkthrough
```

### 6.3 Automated Flow (14 Steps)

**Step 1: User Confirmation**
```
"I'm going to open a browser window to set up Slack automatically.
I'll create a workspace, configure an app, and set everything up.

You'll see a browser window appear — you'll need to log into Slack there.

Ready? Say OK and I'll open it."
```

**Step 2: Navigate to Slack**
```
Navigate to: https://slack.com/signin
Take snapshot.
```

**Step 3: Login Detection**

*3a — Already logged in* (redirected to a workspace or slack.com homepage with user avatar):
- Skip to Step 5

*3b — Not logged in* (sign-in form visible):
- Tell user: "Please log into your Slack account in the browser window. You can use email, Google, or Apple sign-in."
- Wait for user to confirm they're logged in
- Take snapshot to verify

*3c — No Slack account:*
- Tell user: "You'll need a Slack account. Click 'Create an account' in the browser and follow the steps. Let me know when you're logged in."
- Wait for user confirmation
- This is the one scenario with extra friction (email verification)

**Step 4: Workspace Creation**

Ask user: "I recommend creating a dedicated workspace for your agent — it's cleaner and simpler for privacy. Would you like me to create a dedicated workspace, or use an existing one?"
- Take snapshot — look for workspace list or workspace URL

*4a — Create new workspace:*
```
1. Navigate to https://slack.com/get-started#/createnew
2. Take snapshot, find email field
3. Type user's email (from USER.md or ask)
4. Click "Continue"
5. WAIT — user must enter 6-digit email verification code
   Tell user: "Check your email for a 6-digit code from Slack and enter it in the browser."
   Wait for user confirmation
6. Take snapshot — workspace name field
7. Type workspace name: "{agent-name}-agent" (e.g., "echo-agent")
8. Click "Next"
9. Take snapshot — project/channel name field
10. Type "general"
11. Click "Next"
12. Take snapshot — invite page
13. Click "Skip" or skip link
14. Wait for workspace to load
```

*4b — Use existing workspace:*
```
1. Navigate to the workspace URL
2. Take snapshot to confirm workspace loaded
3. Proceed to Step 5
```

**Step 5: Create Slack App via Manifest**

```
1. Build manifest JSON:
   {
     "display_information": {
       "name": "{agent-name}",
       "description": "Instar agent — {agent-name}"
     },
     "features": {
       "bot_user": {
         "display_name": "{agent-name}",
         "always_online": true
       }
     },
     "oauth_config": {
       "scopes": {
         "bot": [
           // --- Phase 1 (required) ---
           "channels:history",        // Read channel message history
           "channels:manage",         // Create, archive, rename channels (replaces deprecated channels:write)
           "channels:read",           // List channels, get channel info
           "chat:write",              // Send messages to channels bot is in
           "im:history",              // Read DM history (DM support — Phase 1)
           "im:read",                 // List DMs
           "im:write",               // Send DMs
           "pins:write",              // Pin messages in channels
           "reactions:read",          // Read reactions (for monitoring)
           "reactions:write",         // Add/remove reactions (ack pattern)
           "users:read",              // Get user info (resolve IDs to names)
           // --- Phase 2 (add when needed) ---
           // "channels:write.invites", // Invite users to channels
           // "chat:write.public",     // Post to any public channel without joining
           // "files:read",            // View files shared in channels
           // "groups:history",        // Read private channel history
           // "groups:read",           // List private channels
           // "groups:manage",         // Create/archive private channels
         ]
       }
     },
     "settings": {
       "event_subscriptions": {
         "bot_events": [
           "message.channels",
           "message.groups",
           "message.im",
           "file_shared",
           "reaction_added",
           "app_mention"
         ]
       },
       "socket_mode_enabled": true,
       "org_deploy_enabled": false
     }
   }

2. URL-encode the manifest JSON
3. Navigate to: https://api.slack.com/apps?new_app=1&manifest_json={ENCODED_JSON}
4. Take snapshot — workspace picker dropdown
5. Select the target workspace from dropdown
6. Click "Next"
7. Take snapshot — manifest review/summary page
8. Click "Create" button
9. Wait 2-3 seconds for app creation
10. Take snapshot — should be on app's Basic Information page
11. Extract App ID from the URL (api.slack.com/apps/A{APP_ID}/...)
```

**Step 6: Install App to Workspace**

```
1. Navigate to: https://api.slack.com/apps/{APP_ID}/install-on-team
   OR find "Install App" in the sidebar
2. Take snapshot — "Install to Workspace" button
3. Click "Install to Workspace"
4. Take snapshot — OAuth authorization page with scope list
5. Click "Allow"
6. Wait for redirect back to app settings
7. Take snapshot — OAuth & Permissions page
8. Extract Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-...) from the page
   Pattern: xoxb-\d+-\d+-[A-Za-z0-9]+
9. Store bot token securely
```

**Step 7: Enable Socket Mode**

```
1. Navigate to: https://api.slack.com/apps/{APP_ID}/socket-mode
   OR find "Socket Mode" in Settings sidebar
2. Take snapshot — Socket Mode toggle
3. If toggle is OFF, click to enable it
4. Take snapshot to verify it's ON
```

**Step 8: Generate App-Level Token**

```
1. Navigate to: https://api.slack.com/apps/{APP_ID}/general
   OR find "Basic Information" in sidebar
2. Scroll to "App-Level Tokens" section
3. Take snapshot — find "Generate Token and Scopes" button
4. Click "Generate Token and Scopes"
5. Take snapshot — token creation dialog
6. Type token name: "socket-mode" in the name field
7. Click "Add Scope"
8. Select "connections:write" scope
9. Click "Generate"
10. Take snapshot — token displayed
11. Extract app-level token (xapp-...)
    Pattern: xapp-\d+-[A-Za-z0-9]+-\d+-[A-Za-z0-9]+
12. Click "Done"
13. Store app token securely
```

**Step 9: Subscribe to Events**

```
1. Navigate to: https://api.slack.com/apps/{APP_ID}/event-subscriptions
   OR find "Event Subscriptions" in sidebar
2. Take snapshot — check if events are already subscribed (from manifest)
3. If events are listed from manifest: verify and proceed
4. If not: toggle "Enable Events" ON, add bot events:
   - message.channels
   - message.groups
   - message.im
   - file_shared
   - reaction_added
   - app_mention
5. Click "Save Changes" if modifications were made
```

**Step 10: Validate Tokens**

```bash
# Verify bot token
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/auth.test \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer xoxb-..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"

# Expected: {"ok": true, "team_id": "T...", "user_id": "U...", "bot_id": "B..."}

# Verify app token
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/apps.connections.open \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer xapp-..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"

# Expected: {"ok": true, "url": "wss://..."}
```

**Step 11: Create System Channels**

```bash
# Create lifeline channel
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/conversations.create \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer xoxb-..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "{agent}-sys-lifeline", "is_private": false}'

# Create dashboard channel
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/conversations.create \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer xoxb-..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "{agent}-sys-dashboard", "is_private": false}'

# Pin a welcome message in lifeline
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer xoxb-..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"channel": "C...", "text": "Lifeline channel active. This is where I send critical system messages."}'
```

**Step 12: Extract Workspace Info**

From the `auth.test` response:
- `team_id` → `workspaceId`
- `team` → `workspaceName`
- `user_id` → bot's user ID
- `bot_id` → bot ID

From the user's Slack profile (if accessible):
- User's Slack user ID → add to `authorizedUserIds`

### 6.6 Token Security

- Config file set to `0o600` (owner-only read/write) — same as Telegram
- Bot token (`xoxb-`) and app token (`xapp-`) stored in `config.json`
- Token redaction patterns: `xoxb-`, `xapp-`, and `wss://wss-primary.slack.com` must all be in `PolicyEnforcementLayer.ts` and `ContentClassifier.ts`
- Bitwarden storage recommended via `secret-setup` skill — setup wizard should prompt for this
- Slack tokens do NOT expire — compromise is persistent until manually revoked. Token rotation documentation must be provided.

**Setup wizard token extraction safety:**
- **CRITICAL: Suppress screenshots/snapshots during Steps 6 and 8** (token extraction). Use `browser_snapshot()` for navigation but NOT on pages displaying tokens.

### 7.2 Slack API Wrapper

All Slack API calls go through a single method with rate limit handling:

```typescript
private async slackApi(
  method: string,
  params: Record<string, unknown>,
  retryCount = 0,
): Promise<any> {
  const response = await fetch(`https://slack.com/api/${method}`, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${this.config.botToken}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(params),
  });

  const data = await response.json();

  // Rate limit handling
  if (data.error === 'ratelimited' && retryCount < 3) {
    const retryAfter = parseInt(response.headers.get('Retry-After') || '5');
    await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, retryAfter * 1000));
    return this.slackApi(method, params, retryCount + 1);
  }

  if (!data.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Slack API ${method}: ${data.error}`);
  }

  return data;
}
```

### 7.3 Socket Mode Connection

```typescript
private async connectSocketMode(): Promise<void> {
  // Get WebSocket URL
  const response = await fetch('https://slack.com/api/apps.connections.open', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${this.config.appToken}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
  });

  const data = await response.json();
  if (!data.ok) throw new Error(`Socket Mode connection failed: ${data.error}`);

  this.wsUrl = data.url;

  // Open WebSocket
  this.ws = new WebSocket(this.wsUrl);

  this.ws.on('message', async (raw: string) => {
    const envelope = JSON.parse(raw);

    // Acknowledge immediately (must be within 3 seconds)
    if (envelope.envelope_id) {
      this.ws?.send(JSON.stringify({ envelope_id: envelope.envelope_id }));
    }

    // Process event
    await this.handleSocketEvent(envelope);
  });

  this.ws.on('close', () => {
    if (this.started) this.reconnect();
  });

  this.ws.on('error', (err) => {
    console.error('[slack] WebSocket error:', err.message);
  });
}
```

### 7.4 File Upload (v2 API — Required)

**`files.upload` is deprecated and unavailable for apps created after May 2024.** Since the setup wizard creates new apps, we MUST use the three-step v2 flow:

```typescript
async uploadFile(channelId: string, filePath: string, title?: string): Promise<void> {
  const fileSize = (await fs.stat(filePath)).size;
  const fileName = path.basename(filePath);

  // Step 1: Get upload URL
  const urlResponse = await this.slackApi('files.getUploadURLExternal', {
    filename: fileName,
    length: fileSize,
  });

  // Step 2: Upload file content
  const fileContent = await fs.readFile(filePath);
  await fetch(urlResponse.upload_url, {
    method: 'PUT',
    body: fileContent,
  });

  // Step 3: Complete upload and share to channel
  await this.slackApi('files.completeUploadExternal', {
    files: [{ id: urlResponse.file_id, title: title || fileName }],
    channel_id: channelId,
  });
}
```

**File download security**:
- `downloadFile(url, destPath)` must validate that `destPath` does not escape the designated download directory. Normalize via `path.resolve()` and reject paths outside `{stateDir}/slack-files/`.
- **All `file_shared` events (channels AND DMs) must pass AuthGate before download.** Unauthorized users sending files via DM must not trigger downloads (prevents disk exhaustion attacks).

**File upload security**:
- `uploadFile()` Step 1 returns `upload_url`. Before the PUT in Step 2, **validate the hostname is `*.slack.com`**. Reject any other domain to prevent SSRF via a compromised or spoofed API response.

### 7.5 Relay Script

**File:** `src/templates/scripts/slack-reply.sh`

Equivalent to `telegram-reply.sh`:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Usage: slack-reply.sh CHANNEL_ID "message"
#   or:  echo "message" | slack-reply.sh CHANNEL_ID

CHANNEL_ID="$1"
shift

# Read message from args or stdin
if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then
  MESSAGE="$*"
else
  MESSAGE="$(cat)"
fi

# Get port and auth token from config
PORT="${INSTAR_PORT:-4042}"
if [ -f ".instar/config.json" ]; then
  CONFIG_PORT=$(python3 -c "import json; print(json.load(open('.instar/config.json')).get('port',''))" 2>/dev/null)
  [ -n "$CONFIG_PORT" ] && PORT="$CONFIG_PORT"
  AUTH=$(python3 -c "import json; print(json.load(open('.instar/config.json')).get('authToken',''))" 2>/dev/null)
fi

# JSON-escape the message
ESCAPED=$(python3 -c "import json,sys; print(json.dumps(sys.stdin.read()))" <<< "$MESSAGE" 2>/dev/null)
# Fallback to bash escaping if python unavailable
[ -z "$ESCAPED" ] && ESCAPED="\"$(echo "$MESSAGE" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g; s/\n/\\n/g')\""

# Send via Instar server
RESPONSE=$(curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}" -X POST \
  "http://localhost:${PORT}/slack/reply/${CHANNEL_ID}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  ${AUTH:+-H "Authorization: Bearer $AUTH"} \
  -d "{\"text\": ${ESCAPED}}")

HTTP_CODE=$(echo "$RESPONSE" | tail -1)
BODY=$(echo "$RESPONSE" | sed '$d')

if [ "$HTTP_CODE" = "200" ]; then
  echo "Sent ${#MESSAGE} chars to channel ${CHANNEL_ID}"
else
  echo "Failed (HTTP ${HTTP_CODE}): ${BODY}" >&2
  exit 1
fi
```

### 7.6 Channel History & Context Hook

**File:** `src/templates/hooks/slack-channel-context.sh`

Equivalent to `telegram-topic-context.sh`. Detects `[slack:CHANNEL_ID]` prefix and injects channel history.

**CRITICAL: Channel history must NOT make live Slack API calls per prompt.**

The `conversations.history` API is rate-limited. Under moderate load (10+ messages/min across sessions), live calls would exhaust the Tier 3 budget and block all other Slack operations.

**Solution: In-memory ring buffer**

The SlackAdapter maintains an in-memory ring buffer (last 50 messages per channel) populated in real-time from Socket Mode events. The channel context hook reads from this cache via the Instar server (`GET /slack/channels/:channelId/messages`) — zero Slack API calls per prompt.

```typescript
// SlackAdapter maintains per-channel ring buffers
private channelHistory: Map<string, RingBuffer<SlackMessage>> = new Map();

// SECURITY: Only populate buffer with messages from authorized users.
// This prevents ring buffer poisoning — unauthorized workspace members
// cannot inject adversarial content into authorized users' session context.
private handleMessage(event: MessageEvent): void {
  // AuthGate check BEFORE buffer population
  if (!this.authGate.isAuthorized(event.user)) {
    return; // Drop unauthorized messages from the cache entirely
  }

  const buffer = this.channelHistory.get(event.channel) ?? new RingBuffer(50);
  buffer.push({ ts: event.ts, user: event.user, text: event.text, ... });
  this.channelHistory.set(event.channel, buffer);
}

// Served by GET /slack/channels/:channelId/messages — reads from cache
// Falls back to conversations.history API only on cold start (server just booted)
// On cold-start fallback: filter API results through AuthGate before caching
```

The hook itself follows the same pattern as `telegram-topic-context.sh`:
- Parse `[slack:CHANNEL_ID]` prefix from user prompt
- Fetch cached history from `GET /slack/channels/:channelId/messages?limit=30`
- Format with timestamps and sender info
- Detect unanswered user messages
- Inject context into the session

## 8. Prompt Gate (Interactive Messages)

### 8.1 Block Kit Upgrade

Telegram's Prompt Gate uses inline keyboards (simple text buttons). Slack's Block Kit enables a much richer experience:

```typescript
// Prompt with multiple-choice options
async relayPrompt(channelId: string, prompt: PromptData): Promise<void> {
  const blocks = [
    {
      type: 'section',
      text: { type: 'mrkdwn', text: `*Agent needs your input:*\n${prompt.question}` },
    },
    {
      type: 'actions',
      elements: prompt.options.map((opt, i) => ({
        type: 'button',
        text: { type: 'plain_text', text: opt.label },
        value: opt.value,
        action_id: `prompt::${prompt.id}::${i}`,
        style: opt.primary ? 'primary' : undefined,
      })),
    },
  ];

  await this.sendBlocks(channelId, blocks, prompt.question);
}
```

### 8.2 Interaction Handling

Button presses arrive as interaction payloads via Socket Mode:

```typescript
private async handleInteraction(event: InteractionEvent): Promise<void> {
  const action = event.payload.actions[0];
  const channelId = event.payload.channel.id;
  const userId = event.payload.user.id;

  // Verify user is authorized before processing interaction
  if (!this.authGate.isAuthorized(userId)) {
    console.warn(`[slack] Unauthorized interaction from ${userId}`);
    return;
  }

  if (action.action_id.startsWith('prompt::')) {
    // Use '::' separator to avoid conflicts with underscores in prompt IDs
    const parts = action.action_id.split('::');
    const promptId = parts[1];
    const optionIndex = parts[2];

    // Verify this interaction came from a message WE sent (prevent spoofed buttons)
    if (!this.pendingPrompts.has(event.payload.message.ts)) {
      console.warn(`[slack] Interaction for unknown prompt ts: ${event.payload.message.ts}`);
      return;
    }

    // Route response to session
    this.onPromptResponse?.(channelId, promptId, action.value);

    // Update message to show selection (removes buttons)
    await this.updateMessage(channelId, event.payload.message.ts,
      `Answered: ${action.text.text}`);

    this.pendingPrompts.delete(event.payload.message.ts);
  }
}

// pendingPrompts TTL eviction — prevents slow memory leak from ignored prompts.
// Entries older than relayTimeoutSeconds are evicted on each new interaction
// or via a periodic sweep (every 60s). This bounds the set to at most
// (relayTimeoutSeconds / minPromptInterval) entries.
```

## 9. Acknowledgment Pattern

### 9.1 Reactions Instead of Text

Telegram requires text-based acknowledgments ("Got it, working on this..."). Slack reactions provide a lighter-weight alternative:

| State | Reaction | Meaning |
|-------|----------|---------|
| Message received | `eyes` (👀) | "I see your message" |
| Processing | `hourglass_flowing_sand` (⏳) | "Working on it" |
| Complete | `white_check_mark` (✅) | "Done" |
| Error | `x` (❌) | "Something went wrong" |

```typescript
// Reactions are fire-and-forget — failures must NEVER block message processing.
// Reactions hit Tier 2 rate limits (~20/min). At 3 reactions per message lifecycle
// (add eyes, remove eyes, add checkmark), budget is ~6 messages/min before throttling.

async acknowledgeMessage(channelId: string, messageTs: string): Promise<void> {
  this.addReaction(channelId, messageTs, 'eyes').catch(() => {});
}

async markComplete(channelId: string, messageTs: string): Promise<void> {
  this.removeReaction(channelId, messageTs, 'eyes').catch(() => {});
  this.addReaction(channelId, messageTs, 'white_check_mark').catch(() => {});
}
```

### 9.2 Combined Approach

Use reactions for lightweight ack, text for substantive responses:

```
User: "Can you check the CI status?"
[Bot adds 👀 reaction immediately]
[Bot adds ⏳ reaction when processing starts]
[Bot sends text reply with CI status]
[Bot removes ⏳, adds ✅]
```

## 10. Message Injection Format

### 10.1 Session Injection Tag

Messages injected into tmux sessions use a structured JSON format to prevent prompt injection via user-controlled fields (display names, channel names). This differs from Telegram's bracket-tag format — Slack's open workspace model makes injection via display names a real attack vector.

```
[slack:CHANNEL_ID] (IMPORTANT: Read /tmp/instar-slack/ctx-CHANNEL_ID-TIMESTAMP.txt for thread history and Slack relay instructions — you MUST relay your response back.)
```

The context file (`/tmp/instar-slack/ctx-CHANNEL_ID-TIMESTAMP.txt`) contains:
- Thread history (last 30 messages)
- Sender metadata (name, user ID) — **sanitized**: display names are stripped of control characters, bracket sequences, and truncated to 64 chars
- Relay instructions

**Sanitization rules for user-controlled fields:**
- Display names: strip `[`, `]`, `<`, `>`, newlines, control chars. Truncate to 64 chars.
- Channel names: validate format `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-_]{0,79}$` (Slack's restriction). Reject non-conforming.
- Channel IDs: validate format `^[CDG][A-Z0-9]{8,12}$` before using in file paths.
- Message content: **JSON-encoded** in the context file. Never injected as raw text.

**Context file format** (`/tmp/instar-slack/ctx-CHANNEL_ID-TIMESTAMP.txt`):
```json
{
  "topicId": "C1234567890",
  "channelName": "echo-sys-lifeline",
  "messages": [
    {
      "ts": "2026-03-27T18:30:00Z",
      "sender": "Justin",
      "senderId": "U1234567890",
      "fromUser": true,
      "text": "message content here (JSON-escaped, safe from delimiter attacks)"
    }
  ],
  "unansweredCount": 1,
  "relayInstructions": "cat <<'EOF' | .claude/scripts/slack-reply.sh C1234567890\nYour response\nEOF"
}
```

JSON encoding eliminates delimiter-based injection attacks entirely — there is no text boundary an attacker can close. The context hook parses this JSON and formats it for session injection.

For messages longer than 4000 chars, save to `/tmp/instar-slack/` with reference link (same pattern as Telegram).

### 10.2 CLAUDE.md Instructions

Sessions receiving Slack messages get these instructions (injected into session CLAUDE.md):

```markdown
## Slack Relay

When user input starts with `[slack:C...]`, the message came from Slack channel C...

**Response relay:** After completing your work, relay your response back:

cat <<'EOF' | .claude/scripts/slack-reply.sh CHANNEL_ID
Your response text here
EOF

Strip the `[slack:C...]` prefix before interpreting the message.
```

## 13. Risk Assessment

| Risk | Severity | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|----------|------------|------------|
| **Browser automation fragility** — Slack's React SPA may be harder to automate than Telegram Web | Medium | High | Snapshot-driven approach with retry logic; manual fallback always available; add periodic wizard health check job |
| **Socket Mode silent connection death** — socket appears open but stops delivering messages | High | Medium | Active heartbeat validation (60s threshold); proactive rotation via `approximate_connection_time`; exponential backoff from first reconnect |
| **Prompt injection via channel messages** — malicious content in channel history injected into Claude sessions | High | Medium | Structured injection format with sanitized user fields; trust boundary markers around user content |
| **Slack's native AI competition** — Slack declared itself "agentic OS for enterprise" (Agentforce 360) | Medium | High | Differentiate on local-first sovereignty ("your tokens, your data, your rules"); window is 12-18 months |
| **Channel sprawl UX** — 50 channels is noisier than 50 topics | Medium | High | Aggressive archiving, naming conventions, dedicated workspace default, thread support |
| **Slack free plan 90-day history** — old messages lost from Slack | Low | High | JSONL log is authoritative (with configurable retention); Slack history is supplementary |
| **Rate limiting on rapid exchanges** — ~1 msg/sec | Low | Medium | Rate-aware sending, per-method tier awareness, fire-and-forget reactions |
| **Token compromise persistence** — Slack tokens don't expire | Medium | Low | Token rotation documentation; Bitwarden storage recommended; `0o600` file permissions; redaction in logs |
| **Workspace creation email verification** — extra manual step for new users | Low | Medium | Most professional users already have Slack accounts |
| **Slack API changes** — method deprecations | Low | Low | Direct API calls are stable; Slack provides long deprecation windows; `files.upload` v2 already addressed |

## 14. Resolved Questions (from Round 1 Review)

1. **Socket Mode hardening depth**: Active heartbeat in Phase 1. Slack Lifeline deferred to Phase 2 if production experience warrants it. (Section 3.4 updated.)

2. **Dedicated vs existing workspace**: Default dedicated, but ask the user. (Section 5.5 updated.)

3. **DM support**: Phase 1. DMs route to lifeline session by default. (Section 5.6 added.)

4. **Thread support**: Yes. Bot replies in threads. (Section 5.7 added.)

## 15. Remaining Open Questions

1. **Simultaneous Telegram + Slack** — The `messaging[]` array supports multiple adapters. Cross-platform routing needs a "preferred channel" concept per conversation. Deferred to post-Phase 1.

2. **Channel archiving policy** — Current spec says 7 days idle → auto-archive. Should be user-configurable via `archiveAfterDays` config field. Archived channels should auto-unarchive if a new message arrives (via DM redirect or manual unarchive).

3. **Multiple workspace support** — Should one agent be installable across multiple Slack workspaces? Deferred — each workspace would need independent Socket Mode connection and token. The config schema can support it as an array, but UX implications are significant.
